<thought>We need to determine how many CH₃ groups are present in the unknown sample. The only way to get structural information is to measure its 13C NMR spectrum (no SMILES needed). By examining the carbon signals in the typical methyl region (≈10–30 ppm) we can count distinct methyl carbons, which corresponds to the number of CH₃ groups. We'll first obtain the 13C NMR spectrum, then retrieve typical carbon shift ranges to identify the methyl region, and finally count the peaks that fall within that range.</thought>
